statement_blocker: The catalog gives only a constructive-proof gloss. Moser-Tardos Theorem 1.2 is the natural source root, but the catalog does not cite or adopt it, distinguish its existential and randomized quantitative conclusions, or exclude the parallel, deterministic, and lopsided variants. No approved mapping fixes the probability model, determining-variable supports, dependency neighborhood, scheduler, resampling process, termination semantics, expected bounds, binders, or boundary cases. Selecting those proposition-changing choices at intake would invent or broaden mathematics.
domain_and_universes: Candidate source domain: finite mutually independent random variables in a probability space, a finite family of bad events determined by finite variable supports, real weights in (0,1), and a randomized sequential resampling execution. Exact value types, measures, supports, schedulers, universes, measurability, arithmetic, and typeclass context remain open.
conclusion: Candidate source conclusion: a satisfying valuation exists, and Algorithm 1.1 reaches one with each bad event and the total number of resamplings bounded in expectation by the stated rational expressions. The exact accepted conclusion and stochastic semantics remain open.
degenerate_case_status: No case is canonically excluded at intake. Source review must resolve every finite-family, probability-law, event-support, dependency, scheduler, termination, expectation, and arithmetic boundary in scope-map.md.
